_comment: Equivalent USDA foods: ingredients a cook would swap for one another, counted as one.
The comparison — and every chart and grid drawn from it — groups each line by the USDA food
it matched. Without this file, four broths match four USDA records and draw four bands.
Each group names the USDA food it is counted as (fdcId) and the USDA foods it stands in for
(members). A line keeps its own match for its grams and sodium; only the grouping changes.
Look ids up in the admin's USDA foods table. A food may sit in one group only, and a group's
own food may not be another group's member.
Seeded 2026-09-30 from the matches of lentil soup, meatloaf and Detroit pizza.

groups.name: Broth and stock
groups.note: Soup, chicken broth, ready-to-serve. Whatever broth is in the fridge — vegetable, chicken or beef, regular or reduced-sodium, home-made stock, bouillon made up with water — opens every soup that calls for any of them; the owner, 2026-09-30, with a non-vegetarian broth as the default. Ready-to-use liquids only: cubes, powders and condensed soup do far more per gram, and fish stock is its own flavour.

groups.name: Lentils
groups.note: Lentils, raw. 'Lentils, dry' and 'pink or red, raw' are uncooked lentils too; the colour is the cook's choice.

groups.name: Wheat flour
groups.note: Wheat flour, white, bread. All-purpose stands in for bread flour in a pan pizza.

groups.name: Butter
groups.note: Butter, without salt. Salted butter's sodium is still counted from its own record.

groups.name: Bread for the binder
groups.note: Bread, crumbs, dry. White bread soaked as a panade does the crumbs' job. 'Bread, pan dulce' is the matcher's reading of plain bread in The Country Cook's meatloaf.

groups.name: Tomatoes
groups.note: Tomatoes, red, ripe, canned. Fresh roma or grape tomatoes in a soup do the canned ones' job. Paste is not here: it is concentrated.

groups.name: Cooking oil
groups.note: Oil, olive. A neutral soybean oil is the same fat for sautéing.

groups.name: Soy sauce
groups.note: Soy sauce (shoyu). Reduced-sodium soy sauce's sodium is still counted from its own record.
